cap: Infections that cross the placenta strike during pregnancy, so prevention protects the mother beforehand through immunity, food safety and syphilis treatment. Infections caught in the birth canal strike at delivery, so prevention happens at delivery: a group B strep culture at 36 to 37 weeks with penicillin in labor, acyclovir and cesarean for herpes, eye ointment, and HBIG with vaccine for hepatitis B.
teach: Herpes simplex sits on the delivery side because most neonatal herpes, about 85 percent, is acquired during birth even though herpes belongs to the TORCH group. Group B strep is Streptococcus agalactiae. Gonococcal conjunctivitis, caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae, appears on days 2 to 5 of life, and chlamydial conjunctivitis on days 5 to 14. HIV and hepatitis B can cross the placenta, but most transmission happens around delivery, which is why delivery-time measures work. Listeria, a gram-positive rod with tumbling motility, is treated with ampicillin because it resists cephalosporins.
